neighbours.label: After a removal or change, the point where what is kept intact is introduced (while leaving most of / but spared most of), vs removing or changing most of it
fire: The dentist removed the decay while leaving most of the tooth in place.
The renovation replaced the roof but left most of the original walls standing.
Careful pruning removes dead branches while sparing most of the healthy canopy.
The fire destroyed the barn yet spared most of the house.
Laser surgery removes the tumour while preserving most of the surrounding tissue.
The flood washed away the bridge but left much of the village untouched.
They cut the budget while keeping most of the staff on the payroll.
The editor trimmed the chapter but kept most of the dialogue.
quiet: The dentist removed most of the tooth and fitted a crown.
The renovation replaced the roof and most of the original walls.
Careful pruning removes most of the dead branches in winter.
The fire destroyed the barn and most of the house.
Laser surgery removes the tumour and most of the surrounding tissue.
The flood washed away the bridge and much of the village.
They cut the budget and laid off most of the staff.
The editor trimmed the chapter and cut most of the dialogue.

predictions: Retention phrases after a removal reach 0.2-0.5 near 'of'/'most'; parallel sentences where most is removed stay under 0.1.
short: what is left intact after a removal
